public_rationale: The firm, sourced part of this claim is that OpenAI's annual compute spend is around $50 billion, per its statements in the Musk trial. Reuters reports that on May 5, 2026, OpenAI president Greg Brockman testified that OpenAI expects to spend $50 billion on computing power this year. That matches the claim. The $100 billion total is hedged with 'appears' and the Anthropic figure with 'likely'. They are estimates, so they are not scored. On the part that can be checked, the claim is supported.
limitations: Only the OpenAI attribution is scored. The total and the Anthropic figure are hedged estimates.
Brockman gave a full-year expectation, not a completed figure.
The source is a news report of testimony, not the court transcript.

our_interpretation: The total ('appears to be roughly $100 billion or so') and the Anthropic figure ('likely spending similar amounts') are openly hedged estimates. They are not scored.
The one firm, sourced statement is that OpenAI's annual compute spend is around $50 billion, 'per their statements in the Musk trial'. That attribution is what gets tested.

Plain reading: in the Musk v. OpenAI trial, an OpenAI representative said OpenAI's annual compute spend is about $50 billion. A full-year 2026 figure, whether projected or actual, fits 'annual compute spend'. No quarterly or run-rate measure is imposed.
Target period: calendar 2026, the 'right now' year of the post and the trial.
criteria.support_condition: A reliable record shows that OpenAI said in the Musk trial that its annual compute spend is about $50 billion, roughly $40 billion to $60 billion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The trial record shows OpenAI gave a materially different annual compute figure, or made no such statement.
